Well, for those of you who haven't heard elsewhere, I recently picked up another project: "Black Fox"

Anyway, here is the new towpig. It's a 1998 Silverado K3500, 454 NV4500 5-speed I bought with 135,000 miles.

Dealership Pictures.....

So, The story goes like this: I've been looking for a new towpig awhile now. I was looking into duramax trucks but I still wanted a manual. After a few months of searching, etc I determined that the cost of owning one VS how much I would use it and the distances I would go just wasn't worth the money. I'd be buying it and wouldn't have any play money to customize it or anything either. So I started looking for GMT400 trucks again.... I ran across this truck about 3.5 hours from me. 1-owner trade in. The dealership listed it as an auto so I hadn't caught it prior. I called, got the pictures, etc etc.... Got the financing figured out. They were asking $9,000, I got them down to bluebook at $7,600 after pointing out some flaws I could see in the pictures. It also has 6 brand new Load E Toyo Open Country AT Tires.

I take the time to drive down there, with money in hand and a friend to drive my 02 back. I took it for a spin and after a few stoplights noticed a whining sound in gears 1 & 2. I later noticed it in Reverse too. The tech checks it, they check fluid. I know it's the bearings in the transmission.... Anyway they looked into it, while they did I grabbed some grub and figured out what I would still pay for it knowing I can' rebuild the transmission myself for a good deal less than they could and I'd have a great truck. So, after the last negotiations, I got the truck for $5,600. It made the 3.5 hour drive home no problems other than the hole in the gas tank

On the way home grabbing some grub. 21' long doesn't fit in many parking stalls.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Or my garage.....
Click this bar to view the full image.


My dog approved, although he was upset I wouldn't let him drive....


And just for all you mid and east coast guys.... Here is what a 15 year old west coast truck looks like underneath.... Not a spec of rust anywhere Ok this truck is particularly clean underneath, even for this area.



So, with that said: Here is the start of my newest project truck, nicknamed "Black Fox". First order of business is to get the trans fixed up and go through the fluids and give it a tune up. Then on to a few towing items, such as removing the current power vision mirrors in favor of the GMT800 towing mirrors, getting a trailer plug wired in (they removed the wiring), and do some cleaning on the paint, wheels, repair the cracked dually fender.... Then eventually onto more "Fun" modifications like Kodiak door handles, Overhead console... etc.

Stay tuned!

Thanks guys!

Welp, the deed has been done. Transmission is pulled from the truck, I'll have to get some pictures. Actually pulled a Getrag from a 90 1st gen Dodge cummins truck, it's getting a NV4500 as well. Was full day of transmission pulling!

Anyway, the trans was as expected inside, needs bearings and synchros. Had a good deal of metal in there. Gears all look fine. Clutch is getting replaced while I'm there.

Also went through a few things, here is the list of items that will be changed in the upcomming months:

- Rebuild transmission with new clutch
- New u-joints and carrier bearing
- Tune up - plugs, wires cap & rotor.
- Injectors. It has the famous leaky vortec injectors that hard start after sitting. Maybe higher flow and a tune.
- Replace broken glovebox
- Wire in trailer connector
- GMT800 towing mirrors
- Tint front windows
- Kodiak Handles
- Re-connect airbags (came with firestones but are disconnected)
- Paint the wheels
- New front lighting & Grille
- Repair/replace LH dually fender (cracked)
- Cut & buff truck, touch up scratches
- Toolbox

I have more things I'm ready to do but we'll leave those up to the imagination.

Compared to the old clutch disc.... It's a little different and a heck of a lot lighter. I'm not quite sure how I feel about it. Seems wimpy.


For comparison... Here is the Hays supertruck that I installed in my 88 about 4 years ago. It's a GREAT clutch. I'm thinking I should swap this AC Delco one out for this instead.... Thoughts?
Click this bar to view the full image.
Subbed for progress. Can't wait to see the outcome on this.
Awesome truck!!

Started tearing into the transmission yesterday. I pulled it and didn't REALLY look at it as it sat in the garage this week.

Top cover off.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Peeking around. Notice the metal shavings. Welp, 5th gear was backing off and the nut wasn't tight...
Click this bar to view the full image.

Click this bar to view the full image.


Drained what was left of the fluid.... This color isn't good.
Click this bar to view the full image.


5th exposed. It's walked back but hasn't contacted the reverse shift arm, no damage.


Popped out the input shaft. I was quite loose and because the pilot bearing had long failed and chewed it up, it was to be replaced anyway. Here is the nose of the mainshaft... Where the input rides on a needle bearing on it...
Click this bar to view the full image.



Damn. This is a showstopper. Planned to have this back together and on the road this weekend. At least I know where the metal was all from now.

Determined that I can still pull the shafts and rebuild the countershaft.

Mainshaft pulled


Countershaft in the housing....


Empty shell.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Counter shaft removed.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Countershaft re-installed with new bearings.



New input shaft


Oh yeah, this wouldn't be possible without this tool set....


Once that was done I set about working on a few other things, such as cleaning my transfercase up.
Click this bar to view the full image.


And my friend (who's also working on his transmission) painted all our drivelines up after I re-built all the u-joints.
Click this bar to view the full image.


And a few more parts to add to the pile.
Throwout bearing/Slave Cylinder.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Tow mirror parts. My current set has a bad heated glass on the driver's side and is missing the post cover on the passenger's side. A friend of mine had his truck stolen and the pass mirror glass was shattered. He ended up replacing the mirrors with a new set and I picked these up off him for parts. Driver's mirror is 100% good. Passenger is for parts only.



Now that I have to buy a mainshaft, I'm at standstill on the transmission itself for a few days. figured I can get some other things taken care of in that time, like the trailer harness, other fluids, mirrors, etc.

Moving along looks good


Sent from my iPhone using Tapatalk - now Free

Originally Posted by Baden
Hey....those look familiar. Good to see they made the trek. I don't trust shipping companies after I worked at UPS and saw some of the stuff that happened, lol.
Yup. Got the two sets together and made one good set. Should be putting them on this weekend.

----------------------

Spent the evening putting all the pieces back together. The trans shop forgot to ship my locking 5th gear nut, so I haven't installed the tail housing yet but will tonight.

For the record, these transmissions are really easy to rebuild. Just have to have the right pullers, installers and a press.






Planning to re-install this in the truck Friday. Then on to other fun mods.

What a weekend!

Spent Friday night putting the truck back together. Got everything done, trans in, clutch bled, etc. Took it out for a test drive. Everything works well, shifts nice.... Until I try 5th gear. It grinds. Every time.... So I play around with it in the driveway... Even sitting still, 5th grinds..... At this point I was SUPER frustrated. After calming down, I research it and determine I put the shift collar for 5th on backwards so it will not engage the synchro.... That means pull things back apart. At least I only have to pull drivelines, transfercase, and the extension housing for the transmission.

So Saturday morning the 2nd tear down...



Here you can see how I had the shift collar installed.
Click this bar to view the full image.


And how it is supposed to go. Taper faced forward.
Click this bar to view the full image.


Here is why.
Click this bar to view the full image.


The taper side has tapered teeth to engage the synchro.
Click this bar to view the full image.

rewrite.rewritten_article_markdown:
In 2013, [88GMCtruck](#user) initiated a project to restore an 1998 Silverado K3500 tow truck, which he named 'Black Fox'. The truck was purchased with approximately 135,000 miles and had six new Load E Toyo Open Country AT Tires. [88GMCtruck](#user) noted that the truck's transmission had bearing issues but managed to get it for a reduced price of $5,600 after negotiations.

[88GMCtruck](#user) detailed several modifications planned for 'Black Fox', including rebuilding the transmission with new clutch and bearings, installing towing mirrors, wiring in a trailer plug, and cleaning the paint. Additionally, various parts such as gloveboxes, u-joints, front windows, and HVAC systems were replaced or updated.

The transmission rebuild process involved significant work, including removing and reassembling several components like the input shaft, countershaft, and shift collar. The truck underwent a full restoration, with improvements to both the exterior and interior. [88GMCtruck](#user) also shared details about parts sourced from another project vehicle and junkyard finds.

The final stages included installing heated mirrors, front Kodiak handles, and de-badging the truck. [Scott Long](#user) later inquired about fuel efficiency, to which [88GMCtruck](#user) confirmed good overall performance with a 12.8 MPG on long-distance trips.

This project showcases [88GMCtruck](#user)'s dedication and skill in restoring classic trucks for towing purposes.

post_rewrites.rewritten_content:
I recently acquired another project vehicle: a 1998 Silverado K3500 with a 454 NV4500 5-speed manual transmission, clocking 135,000 miles. It was listed at the dealership as an automatic but turned out to be a manual. I bought it for $7,600 after negotiating from their asking price of $9,000.

The truck is in excellent condition with six new Load E Toyo Open Country AT tires. During my test drive, I noticed a whining sound in first and second gears, confirmed to be transmission bearings by the tech. I opted for a deal at $5,600, driving it home without issues except a hole in the gas tank.

This GMT400 truck is now named "Black Fox." My first steps will involve fixing the transmission, changing fluids, and performing a tune-up. Upcoming tasks include installing GMT800 towing mirrors, wiring a trailer plug, cleaning the paint and wheels, and repairing the cracked dually fender. I also plan to add more fun modifications like Kodiak door handles and an overhead console.

Stay tuned for updates!
I'm impressed by how cleanly it is underneath.
CKTA noted that the underside is exceptionally clean. They express surprise and enthusiasm, wishing their own 2004 model were in such good condition. They also praise the find as a great discovery.
My 1988 model is nearly as clean on the inside, despite having 205,000 miles.
It looks great. Let's move on to the more fun additions.
I'm definitely envious of how clean it appears. I've subscribed.

Thanks everyone! The transmission has been successfully removed from a 1990s first-gen Dodge Cummins truck, and it's getting an NV4500 replacement. It was a full day of work!

The transmission is in need of new bearings and synchronizers, with some metal debris inside. The clutch will be replaced during this process.

Future tasks include:
- Rebuilding the transmission with a new clutch
- Installing new U-joints and carrier bearing
- Performing a tune-up: spark plugs, wires, caps, and rotors
- Replacing leaky Vortec injectors with higher-flow units and tuning
- Fixing the broken glove box
- Wiring in a trailer connector
- Installing GMT800 towing mirrors
- Tinting the front windows
- Adding Kodiak handles
- Reconnecting airbags, which came with Firestone tires but are currently disconnected
- Painting the wheels
- Upgrading front lighting and grille
- Repairing or replacing the cracked left-hand dually fender
- Cutting, buffing, and touch-up scratches on the truck
- Refinishing the toolbox

There are additional projects I plan to tackle, though they'll remain a surprise.
A few dollars' worth of parts were used—specifically, three transmissions and two transfer cases. Click the bar to view the full image. Here is what was removed from my truck.

Several components have arrived. Here are the details:

- Combine these with the two I retained from my 99 K2500.
- Full view: All movable parts from the NV4500, excluding gears and shafts.
Sent from my iPhone using Tapatalk

Today, I received items via Amazon's two-day shipping: U-joints, a carrier bearing, and trailer wiring. The U-joints are installed, and I'll replace the carrier bearing with my dad tomorrow.

I also got a suburban rear Weathetech mat from the '88, which fits adequately but isn't as snug against the rear seat frame as desired.

A new clutch kit arrived; it's lighter but feels less substantial than the old one. For comparison, I've installed a Hays supertruck clutch in my '88 for four years, and it performs excellently. Considering swapping the AC Delco clutch with the Hays model. Any thoughts? 

![](full_image_link)
Subbed for progress. Excited to see the outcome.
Amazing truck!

Yesterday, I began disassembling the transmission, noticing metal shavings and an issue with 5th gear where the nut wasn't tight. The fluid was drained, revealing poor quality. Inspection showed minimal wear on the 5th gear and a loose input shaft due to a failed pilot bearing. I removed the mainshaft and countershaft, finding them in need of new bearings and replacement. 

Additional tasks included cleaning the transfer case and updating trailer and vehicle fluids. Tow mirror parts were also sourced from a friend’s stolen truck, with the passenger side being needed for parts only.

With the mainshaft to be rebuilt, I'll focus on other necessary repairs like the trailer harness and other fluids over the next few days.
Progress appears to be going well. Sent from my iPhone via Tapatalk - currently free.
Those packages look familiar. It's good to see they arrived safely. After working at UPS, I'm not entirely trusting of shipping companies.

Originally Posted by Baden

Those transmissions look familiar. It’s good to see they arrived safely.

After working at UPS, I don’t fully trust shipping companies, but these trans rebuilds went smoothly with the right tools—pullers, installers, and a press.

I’ve reassembled all components. The shop forgot to include my locking 5th gear nut, so I haven’t installed the tail housing yet, but I’ll do that tonight.

These transmissions are quite easy to rebuild. I plan to reinstall this one in the truck on Friday, then move on to other modifications.

What an eventful weekend! I spent Friday night reassembling my truck, including installing the transmission and bleeding the clutch. A test drive went smoothly, but 5th gear was problematic; it would grind every time. Upon further investigation, I realized I had installed the shift collar for 5th gear incorrectly, preventing proper engagement with the synchro. Disappointing though this was, at least I only needed to拆卸变速箱、分动箱和传动轴。Saturday morning saw me disassembling again to correct the mistake.

Here’s a visual of my initial installation and how it should have been:

![](images/collar_installed.jpg)
![](images/correct安装方式.jpg)

The taper side features teeth that engage with the synchro, which is crucial for smooth gear changes. After reassembly, everything worked as expected. The transmission now shifts smoothly.

I took a 250-mile trip to break in the truck and achieved an impressive 12.8 MPG at highway speeds between 70-80 MPH. Not bad at all!

Upon returning home, I tackled some updates:

- Replaced tailgate cables with solid straps for added security.
- Installed a center console in place of the rear armrest, which was cheaply priced at $3.74.
- Acquired steering wheel audio controls and an HVAC system with rear defrost.

I also removed wheels to paint them black, installed chrome caps, and removed trim rings for now. Lastly, I fitted power heated signal/parking light tow mirrors and front Kodiak handles (rear ones awaited door rods). The truck is now de-badged as well.

More modifications are on the horizon, including window tinting, light smoking, and deciding on headlight treatments.

The truck looks great. What fuel efficiency are you seeing? I opted for the Hays clutch kit instead of the AC Delco model, as it seemed more robust. Have you considered blacking out the bumpers? Chrome bumpers painted with plastidip appear good, but glossy black painted steel might match the truck better. The rear seat legroom is impressive.

Scott Long's post has been refined as follows:

The truck looks great. What gas mileage are you seeing? I opted for the Hays clutch kit instead of the AC Delco model; it seemed stronger. For the bumpers, I plan to use PlastiDip initially, with painted steel ones potentially later for a more polished look. The rear seat leg room is impressive—it’s an original equipment part and should suffice.

I’ve ordered new parts for a tune-up: spark plugs, wires, cap, rotor, fuel pressure regulator, and Bosch injectors. The current spark plugs are overdue for replacement.
